changes: Core counted file reads allocate no more than the remaining expected bytes plus one growth-detection byte, capped at the existing chunk limit. Every file and EOF is still read.
Installed tests cover unchanged digests, empty and multichunk files, growth, truncation, dependency coverage, composition, native bridges and lease behavior.
Nexus and Connector pin the same Core 0.2.44 wheel. Nexus inventory version, checked-in wheel and frozen lock agree.
The real provider journey now invokes the public Connector CLI in separate Python processes and fails immediately on a durable Core event-observation incident.

measurements.caveat: Baseline used cProfile (17.706 s); the bounded-read diagnostic did not (5.084 s). These are diagnostic timings, not a controlled benchmark or end-to-end latency guarantee.

findings: The first consumer run refused Core 0.2.44 because Nexus inventory still pinned 0.2.43. The inventory pin was corrected and the final Nexus wheel rebuilt; the failed report and previous artifact remain.

Pi subsequently opened and renewed its lease, but a same-loop CLI run lost native event observation. Thread-isolated CLI completed a turn with an OPEN handoff; CLI subprocesses completed a turn with a CLAIMED handoff. These remain failures.

A diagnostic response hook observed valid HTTP 200 native action responses and produced one complete Pi journey. It read response bodies before the production validator; this instrumented pass is excluded from acceptance.

The final Pi repetition removed that hook and failed on core.event_pump_failed. It ran concurrently with the independent installed regression suite. The daemon exited normally and campaign credentials were removed.

Codex and Claude passed on final wheels with actual CLI subprocesses, lease renewal, three explicit operator decisions each, completed handoffs, successful turn and close receipts, normal shutdown and credential cleanup.

The frozen offline Nexus install succeeded in an isolated CPython 3.14.3 environment; imports resolve Core 0.2.44 from site-packages with Connector absent. This is packaging evidence, not a real embedded provider journey.
limitations: Pi remains unaccepted. Root causes of event loss and native action uncertainty are not yet established; a successful instrumented run does not resolve intermittent failures.
Server release readiness is overridden only by the test; native provider qualification is unchanged.
This campaign uses one Windows host and loopback HTTP/WSS, not independent hosts, Linux, deployed TLS or UI.
Core 0.2.44 introduces no native action timeout, buffer limit, authorization or qualification relaxation.
Nexus UI assets were preexisting changes carried by its built wheel; they remain outside commits and UI acceptance.
Counts overlap across source, installed and historical campaigns. G0-G3 and M00-M13 remain open.
next_step: Capture the concrete exception behind Pi core.event_pump_failed, reproduce it with bounded native event ingestion tests, and correct the cause. Also measure metadata validation relative to the native ingress observation budget; preserve same-action recovery and authority checks.
